S67.01.needs: Desktop app with a folder on this computer added
S67.01.note: The Explore the project button sends a fixed prompt that asks for the project's purpose and main files.
steps: Click Add a folder and choose a project folder on this computer.
Click New session in that folder.
In the Start a coding task area, click Explore the project.
Read the reply. It should name the main folders, entry points and how they connect, as Expected says.
S67.01.where: Code > On this device > Add a folder, then New session in that folder > Start a coding task > Explore the project

S67.02.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session
S67.02.note: No separate control; this is a free-form question to the agent.
steps: Open a local session for the folder.
Click the Continue this session box and type: Where is <function or name> implemented? Give the file and line.
Click Send.
Check that the reply names the defining file and line.
S67.02.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Continue this session (composer)

S67.03.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session
S67.03.note: No separate control; this is a free-form question to the agent.
steps: Open a local session for the folder.
Type in the Continue this session box: Where is <symbol> used across the repository?
Click Send.
Check that the reply lists references in several files.
S67.03.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Continue this session (composer)

S67.04.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session
S67.04.note: No separate control; this is a free-form question to the agent.
steps: Open a local session for the folder.
Type in the Continue this session box: Trace how <button or action> flows from the UI to the code it changes.
Click Send.
Check that the reply walks from the entry point to the final effect, with file names.
S67.04.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Continue this session (composer)

S67.05.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session
S67.05.note: No separate control; this is a free-form question to the agent.
steps: Open a local session for the folder.
Type any question about the project in the Continue this session box.
Click Send.
Check that the answer is based on the project's files.
S67.05.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Continue this session (composer)

S67.06.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session; a writable test folder
S67.06.note: Ask mode asks before each edit, so use Auto to see edits without prompts.
steps: Open a local session for the folder.
Set Permissions to Auto. The shortcut is Cmd+Shift+M on a Mac.
Type a feature request in the Continue this session box and click Send.
Click Review changes and check that new or edited files appear.
S67.06.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Permissions (set to Auto) > Continue this session (composer)

S67.07.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session; a test folder with a known bug
S67.07.note: No separate control; the fix is made through the agent.
steps: Open a local session for the folder.
Set Permissions to Auto.
Type a bug description and the steps to reproduce it in the Continue this session box, then click Send.
Click Review changes and check that the fix touches the file that causes the bug.
S67.07.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Permissions (set to Auto) > Continue this session (composer)

S67.08.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session
S67.08.note: No separate control; the refactor is requested through the agent.
steps: Open a local session for the folder.
Set Permissions to Auto.
Type: Refactor <module> into smaller parts without changing behaviour. Click Send.
Click Review changes and run Run tests to check behaviour is unchanged.
S67.08.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Permissions (set to Auto) > Continue this session (composer)

S67.09.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session
S67.09.note: No separate control; tests are requested through the agent.
steps: Open a local session for the folder.
Set Permissions to Auto.
Type: Write tests for <function>. Click Send.
Click Review changes and check that a new test file or new test cases appear.
S67.09.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Permissions (set to Auto) > Continue this session (composer)

S67.10.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session; a folder with a test script
S67.10.note: If no test command exists, the message says No test command found here.
steps: Open a local session for a folder that has a test command.
Click the Run tests button in the session header.
Watch the status line: Running <command>.
Check the result: <command> passed., or failed with exit code, and read Test output.
S67.10.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Run tests (header button)

S67.11.needs: Desktop app; a folder with a failing test
S67.11.note: No separate control; the interpretation is requested through the agent.
steps: Run tests on a folder where a test fails.
Open Test output and read the failure.
Type in Continue this session: Explain why these tests fail and fix the cause. Click Send.
Check that the reply names the failing test and cause, and that Review changes shows any fix.
S67.11.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Run tests (header button) > Continue this session (composer)

S67.12.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session; a folder with a type checker
S67.12.note: No dedicated type-check button; the check is requested through the agent.
steps: Open a local session for a TypeScript folder.
Type in Continue this session: Run the project's type checker and list the errors. Click Send.
Check that the reply reports the checker's errors with file names, or states there are none.
S67.12.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Continue this session (composer)

S67.13.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session; a folder with a linter
S67.13.note: No dedicated lint button; the check is requested through the agent.
steps: Open a local session for the folder.
Type in Continue this session: Run the project's linter and list the findings. Click Send.
Check that the reply reports the lint output with file names.
S67.13.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Continue this session (composer)

S67.14.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session; a folder with a build command
S67.14.note: No dedicated build button; the build runs as a typed terminal command.
steps: Open a local session for the folder.
Click the Terminal panel button in the session header.
Click New terminal and type the project's build command, then press Return.
Check that the terminal ends with the build's output and exit status.
S67.14.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Terminal panel > New terminal

S67.15.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session; a folder with a dev server command
S67.15.note: The keep-running behaviour is partly visible in the close prompt text; the agent's own use of the server is not shown in the UI.
steps: Open a local session and click the Terminal panel button.
Click New terminal and type the project's dev server command, then press Return.
Ask the agent in Continue this session for a small edit and click Send, while the server keeps running.
Check that the server stays up. Closing its tab should ask: Close this terminal? and say it is still running here.
S67.15.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Terminal panel > New terminal

S67.16.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session; a running local web app for the URL
S67.16.note: The page is shown in the Browser pane; the agent's own inspection steps are not shown in the pane.
steps: Open a local session and click the Browser button in the header.
Click Web address, type a local URL such as localhost:3000, and press Return.
Use Back, Forward and Reload to check the pages load.
Ask the agent in Continue this session to check the page, and read the reply.
S67.16.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Browser (header button)

S67.17.needs: a paired Chrome browser for the agent step
S67.17.note: No console panel found in apps/web/features/code/components/LocalBrowserPanel.tsx. The console step exists as device_browser_console in packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/device-steps.ts:289 for the paired Chrome browser, and the user is asked before it runs. Not confirmed as a visible control.

S67.18.needs: a paired Chrome browser for the agent step
S67.18.note: The network step exists as device_browser_network in packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/device-steps.ts:294 for the paired Chrome browser. No network panel found in LocalBrowserPanel.tsx.

S67.20.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session that has uncommitted changes
S67.20.note: The /review command's description, Review the changes in this session for bugs, is in apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts.
steps: Make a change in the folder, then open a local session.
Click Review changes in the header and check the changed files.
Type /review in Continue this session and click Send.
Check that the findings name file and line, as Expected says.
S67.20.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Continue this session (composer) > type /review

S67.21.needs: A GitHub account with the AGI GitHub App installed on a repository, and a pull request
S67.21.note: The GitHub card name is taken from the connector data and was not checked on screen. The review is posted by the GitHub webhook route at apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts.
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors.
Find the GitHub connector and turn on Review pull requests.
Open a pull request on that repository and wait for it to open.
Check that AGI posts a review as a comment on the pull request.
S67.21.where: Settings > Connectors > GitHub > Review pull requests

labels.text: Check the changes in this session for security problems

S67.22.needs: A paid plan with Code, and a cloud session with a repository
S67.22.note: The /security-review command is in the cloud composer. Not confirmed for the local composer.
steps: Click Code in the sidebar and open a cloud session that has changes.
In the composer, type /security-review and pick it from the list.
Click Send.
Check that the reply lists security problems with their location.
S67.22.where: Code > Cloud sessions > open a session > Continue (composer) > type /security-review

S67.23.needs: A session that has run /review or /security-review
S67.23.note: No separate findings view was found; findings appear in the agent's reply.
steps: After S67.20 or S67.22 finishes, open the same session.
Read the reply in the transcript.
Check that each finding has a plain explanation and a file and line.
S67.23.where: Code > open the session after a review or scan > read the reply in the transcript

S67.24.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session
S67.24.note: The Plan mode description is in LOCAL_AGENT_MODE_HINTS in apps/web/features/code/local-code.ts.
steps: Open a local session and set Permissions to Plan.
Type in Continue this session: Propose a fix for <issue>, do not change any files. Click Send.
Read the proposed change in the reply. Check Review changes shows no edits.
Set Permissions to Ask, ask again, and check the Approval required card with Approve and continue appears before any edit.
S67.24.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Permissions (set to Plan) > Continue this session (composer)

S67.25.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session that has several changed files
S67.25.note: Hunk-level Stage and Revert also exist. The cloud Changes panel has Include in the commit checkboxes in apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts.
steps: Open a local session with several changed files and click Review changes.
Click Stage file on one file only.
Check the status says Staged 1 change. and that other files are not staged.
Click Revert file on another file, confirm Revert these changes?, and check only that file changes back.
S67.25.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Review changes > Stage file or Revert file

S67.26.needs: Desktop app with a local folder session
S67.26.note: No dedicated documentation button; the request is made through the agent.
steps: Open a local session with Permissions set to Auto.
Type in Continue this session: Write or update the README section for <module> from the code. Click Send.
Click Review changes and open the README or doc comment changes.
Check the new text matches the code.
S67.26.where: Code > On this device > open a session > Continue this session (composer)

S67.27.needs: the desktop app and a git repository folder on this Mac
S67.27.note: There is no migration button; the agent does it from a chat request, so the tester checks the agent's output, not a control.
steps: Sign in to the desktop app and click Code in the sidebar.
If no folder is listed, click Add a folder and pick a git repository folder on this Mac.
Click New session in [folder name] under that folder.
Type a migration task, for example: Rename every use of the old config key to the new key, and send.
Look at the reply and the Changes pane: the agent names the files it changed, and those files now show the new name.
S67.27.where: Code > Add a folder (if none is open) > New session in [folder name] > type the migration task and send

S67.28.needs: the desktop app, a folder on this Mac with a package manifest, and network access for the package registry
S67.28.note: There is no upgrade button; this depends on the agent running the install in the folder, so the tester checks its output.
steps: Sign in to the desktop app, click Code and open a session in a folder that has a package manifest (for example package.json).
Type an upgrade task, for example: Upgrade one outdated dependency to its latest version and fix any code that breaks, and send.
Wait for the agent to finish, then open the Changes pane.
Compare: the manifest and the code files the agent changed are listed, and the agent reports the new version it installed.
S67.28.where: Code > Add a folder (if none is open) > New session in [folder name] > type the upgrade task and send

labels.text: Stages and reverts changes. Run git commit in your terminal to commit.

S67.29.needs: the desktop app and a git repository folder on this Mac
S67.29.note: The agent commits with its git_commit tool. The Commit message and Commit and push form is on the cloud Code page, not in a local folder session.
steps: Click Code, then New session in [folder name].
Type a small change request, for example: Add one line to README.md, and send. Wait for the change.
Type: Commit these changes with the message Add README note, and send.
If a commit hook runs, a prompt asks you to allow it. Answer it.
Compare: the agent reports the commit. Open Changes: a line reads Stages and reverts changes. Run git commit in your terminal to commit. when you commit by hand.
S67.29.where: Code > New session in [folder name] > type a commit request in the message box and send

labels.text: Create branch and open pull request

S67.30.needs: the desktop app and a git repository folder on this Mac
S67.30.note: The agent creates the branch with git_branch_create, which does not switch to it. The button Create branch and open pull request shows only when the folder is not on a branch (LocalPullRequest.tsx).
steps: Click Code, then New session in [folder name] on a folder that is a git repository.
Type: Create a branch named qa-branch-test for this work, and send.
Compare: the agent reports the new branch name.
Open Changes and check the branch name shown in the session group in the sidebar, or ask the agent: Which branch are we on?
S67.30.where: Code > New session in [folder name] > type a branch request in the message box and send

labels.text: Push and open a pull request
Open a pull request on GitHub

S67.31.needs: a GitHub account connected to AGI, and a git folder with a GitHub remote; without the AGI GitHub App on that repository, the button opens the GitHub compare page instead
S67.31.note: The pull request block is inside the Changes pane (LocalChangesPanel.tsx); the Create branch and open pull request button appears instead when the folder is on no branch.
steps: Click Code and open a session in a git folder that is on a branch other than the default branch and has a GitHub remote.
Make a change with the agent so there is something to push.
Click Changes in the session header.
Click Push and open a pull request below the file list.
Compare: a Pull request # link appears with a checks status. Clicking it opens the pull request on GitHub.
S67.31.where: Code > [session in a folder] > Changes > Push and open a pull request

S67.34.note: Code line says partial: the switch-on is an E2B sandbox gate (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts). I searched apps/web for issue_comment, app_mention and mention triggers and found no UI path that starts coding from a GitHub issue or team mention.

S67.37.needs: a folder on this computer, and memory turned on for the account (the Memory button is hidden otherwise and in remote SSH sessions)
S67.37.note: The button shows only when runtimeModels.features.memory is true (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalSessionPanel.tsx).
steps: Click Code and open a session in a folder.
Click the Memory button in the session header (brain icon, tooltip Memory).
Type a repository fact, for example: Tests run with the npm test script. Choose Project memory and click Save to memory.
Compare: the line Saved to appears with a file path.
Open a new session in the same folder and ask: How do we run the tests? The answer should use the saved fact.
S67.37.where: Code > [session in a folder] > Memory button (brain icon, tooltip Memory) > What to remember > Save to memory

S67.38.needs: a folder on this computer with an AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md file
S67.38.note: The instruction files are loaded by the CLI loader (apps/cli/src/compaction.rs load_instructions); the desktop app path was not confirmed in the cited dispatcher lines.
steps: Create AGENTS.md in a test folder with one rule, for example: Always answer in one word.
Click Code and open a new session in that folder.
Ask a question such as: What is the capital of France?
Compare: the reply follows the rule from AGENTS.md. In the terminal CLI, /memory shows what the session loads.
S67.38.where: No control. Seen in a new session in a folder that has an AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md file

S67.39.needs: the desktop app, a folder open in a local session, and a folder or account that has at least one skill or plugin
S67.39.note: The button shows in every local session header (LocalSessionPanel.tsx line 1067); the list is empty when no skill or plugin is installed.
steps: Click Code and open a session in a folder that has a skill or plugin.
Click the Skills and plugins button in the session header (sparkle icon).
If a project skill is listed and not trusted, read the note and click Trust this folder's skills.
Turn one skill's switch off, then on. Each row shows the name and its scope, under Skills or Plugins.
Compare: a switched-off skill is not used when you ask for it, and a failed change shows That change could not be saved.
S67.39.where: Code > [session in a folder] > Skills and plugins button (sparkle icon, tooltip Skills and plugins) > turn a switch on or off
